answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may place jobs or claim rewards. A reputation system then raises the stake or waiting period for accounts with no verified history, while slashing deposits for provable fraud. Splitting one operator across a hundred agents no longer creates influence cheaply: the attacker must tie up capital in every identity and risk losing it. An ember of trust is earned slowly, not minted by naming a new account; the jetty and wharf still need real cargo.
